messages.content: I want to pressure-test the flights before I buy. Compare the full itineraries, including connections and bag charges, and make sure the Tuesday flight is actually reachable from Easton.

The cleanest pairing is the $512 Delta round trip: Sunday MSP 5:10 p.m.-CMH 8:03 p.m., nonstop, 1 hour 53 minutes; Tuesday CMH 6:35 p.m.-MSP 7:42 p.m., nonstop, 2 hours 7 minutes. Carry-on and personal item are included. One standard checked bag is $35 each way, so $70 round trip.

The lowest fare is $367 on United: Sunday MSP 4:18 p.m.-ORD 5:52 p.m., then ORD 8:09 p.m.-CMH 10:41 p.m.; total time 5 hours 23 minutes with a 2 hour 17 minute connection. Tuesday leaves CMH at 5:15 p.m., connects in ORD for 58 minutes, and reaches MSP at 9:24 p.m. Carry-on is included; the quoted first-bag charge is $35 each way.

There is also a $449 mixed pairing using Sunday’s nonstop and Tuesday’s 5:15 p.m. United connection. It improves Sunday but does not fix the tight Tuesday departure.
That 5:15 return sounds doubtful. Meetings can run until 4:10, and I would still need to get downstairs and call the ride.

I would rule it out. A realistic sequence is leaving the office around 4:15, waiting 5-10 minutes for the rideshare, and spending roughly 10-20 minutes in traffic to CMH. That puts you at the terminal around 4:30-4:45 for a 5:15 departure. With a checked bag, the likely 45-minute bag cutoff could already be missed; with carry-on only, the margin is still too thin for traffic, security, or a meeting overrun.
Is the 6:35 nonstop comfortably reachable, or are we still stretching it?

It is reasonable. Using the same conservative assumptions, you should reach CMH around 4:45, leaving about 1 hour 50 minutes before departure. Even a 20-minute additional delay would leave roughly 90 minutes. You should arrange the pickup in advance, leave the office immediately when the meeting ends, and avoid a stop between Easton and the airport.
What would the one-stop outbound save, and what does it cost me besides the later arrival?

Against the $512 nonstop pairing, the $367 United itinerary saves $145 before baggage. The tradeoff is 3 hours 30 minutes of additional Sunday travel, a Chicago connection, and arrival at 10:41 p.m. instead of 8:03 p.m. After deplaning and the rideshare, hotel arrival would likely be around 11:15-11:30 p.m. It also forces the unreliable 5:15 Tuesday return, so I would not treat the $367 fare as viable for this schedule.
Could I combine that United outbound with the 6:35 return and stay under my $525 airfare ceiling?

That combination prices at $486 round trip: United through ORD on Sunday, then the 6:35 nonstop Tuesday. It is under the ceiling by $39 and the Tuesday margin works. With one checked bag each way, airfare plus bags would be $556. The all-nonstop $512 pairing is also under the airfare ceiling, but becomes $582 with the same bag charges.
So the practical comparison is $486 with a long Sunday connection versus $512 for nonstop both ways. Correct?

Correct. The fare difference is only $26. Both use the reachable 6:35 Tuesday departure and both remain below the $525 airfare ceiling. The $486 option adds a 2 hour 17 minute ORD connection and reaches Columbus 2 hours 38 minutes later on Sunday. Unless the $26 matters more than the lost evening and connection risk, the $512 all-nonstop itinerary is the stronger choice.

Use the $512 nonstops. One broader correction for future searches: replace the Delta preference. Include United among the carriers you compare when it fits the trip, but United is not required and should not beat another comparable option just because of the name.

Understood. For future flight comparisons, I’ll include United when its itinerary is suitable, without treating it as mandatory or giving it an automatic ranking advantage. For Columbus, the selected working choice remains the Delta nonstop pairing because its schedule and $26 premium are materially better than the viable United combination.
Give me the final flight schedule, Tuesday timing, and revised trip total. Keep it explicitly unbooked.

Working plan, not booked: Sunday, December 9, depart MSP nonstop at 5:10 p.m. and arrive CMH at 8:03 p.m. Rideshare to the Hilton Columbus at Easton for two nights. Tuesday, December 11, take your carry-on to the Easton office, request the rideshare as the meeting wraps, and leave by about 4:15 p.m. Expected terminal arrival is 4:30-4:45 p.m.; depart CMH nonstop at 6:35 p.m. and arrive MSP at 7:42 p.m.

The estimated trip total remains $1,098: $512 airfare, $458 room charge, about $80 hotel tax, and about $48 for rides. If you check one bag each way, add $70, bringing the estimate to $1,168. Before purchase, confirm the $512 fare, exact flight times, baggage fee, and Tuesday operating schedule; also confirm the hotel’s taxed total, availability, cancellation deadline, and the office rideshare pickup point. Nothing has been booked.

The Tuesday plan is to leave the Easton office around 4:15 p.m. after meetings end, rideshare directly to CMH, and arrive around 4:30-4:45 p.m.; the 5:15 p.m. return was ruled out as unreliable.
